The route will be relatively flat, with an elevation gain of 59 metres over a total distance of 9.4 kilometres. Motorsport enthusiasts will recognise the Monaco Grand Prix circuit, which forms a significant part of the route. The riders will pass through the Place du Casino, the famous Fairmont bend and the Louis II tunnel before arriving on Boulevard Albert 1er, where the victory cries of drivers such as Ayrton Senna, Alain Prost, Michael Schumacher, Fernando Alonso, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli still echo."],"stage":1,"stageType":"PAS","highlight":false,"publicationAt":"2026-08-22T16:14:48+02:00","_id":"6dc5367e1bea2fcd9489b530f04836de5e10b1126404b676be27f94f51a18a6c","_bind":"publication_en-2026-1","_origin":"news-2026-1","_updatedAt":1787408089148,"_parent":"stage-2026:93bd5639e913abc271fb13124da9db9a6a602ca76973eeae9a729197feefbbdb","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:following-the-tracks-of-formula-1-legends","model":"news"},{"stageType":"PAS","stage":1,"highlight":false,"type":"liv","pinned":false,"updatedBy":"bvittek","id":51201,"year":2026,"text":["The start in Monaco features a very special participant: Monegasque rider Victor Langelloti (XDS Astana), the only rider from the Principality in the current professional peloton, who will begin his third appearance in La Vuelta on home soil.
“As a Monegasque, it is an honour to be able to ride La Vuelta at home and a source of pride to be able to wear this jersey”, says Langellotti, who won both the road race and the ITT at the national championships. “In 2009, when the Tour de France started from here, as a local cyclist I was able to accompany Alberto Contador’s Astana team at the team presentation. After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn.
With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. A few weeks later, Cancellara was the first leader of the 2009 Vuelta after an ITT in Assen (the Netherlands)."],"_id":"7496e3db0d627eafa45ce6c2191a4a18fcfd19d6632c34680901e1ce9a9d78a6","_bind":"publication_en-2026-1","_origin":"news-2026-1","_updatedAt":1787406708698,"_parent":"stage-2026:93bd5639e913abc271fb13124da9db9a6a602ca76973eeae9a729197feefbbdb","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:welcome-to-monaco","model":"news"},{"createdBy":"bvittek","stage":1,"updatedAt":"2026-08-22T16:32:05+02:00","publicationAt":"2026-08-22T16:32:05+02:00","createdAt":"2026-08-22T16:32:05+02:00","text":["15 stage wins - Primoz Roglic

Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) is set to be the first rider on course, from 16:17, as he participates in his first Grand Tour. At 24, he is in his third season as a professional, after developing with Lizarte, Kern Pharma’s feeder club.
He will be followed at 16:18 later by the much more experienced Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL), lining up for the sixth time at the start of La Vuelta.
The 184 contenders of this edition will start every minute, finishing wit some of the most awaited champions in this edition. Belgian icon Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) will go at 19:17. He will be followed by Spain’s rising star Ivan Romeo (Movistar). After them, two Slovenian giants will close the action: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG), starting at 19:19, and Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), a minute after his compatriot."],"pinned":false,"slug":"from-uriarte-to-roglic","_id":"94d2c1ecc791a4ef21f2a5ee8999ca4aebe5702e66d2365ec2fa4a29d98d4005","_bind":"publication_en-2026-1","_origin":"news-2026-1","_updatedAt":1787407722561,"_parent":"stage-2026:93bd5639e913abc271fb13124da9db9a6a602ca76973eeae9a729197feefbbdb","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:from-uriarte-to-roglic","model":"news"},{"createdAt":"2026-08-22T16:36:12+02:00","stage":1,"id":51311,"createdBy":"bvittek","text":["16:37 - Orluis Aular, Venezuela

Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) is set to be the first rider on course, from 16:17, as he participates in his first Grand Tour. At 24, he is in his third season as a professional, after developing with Lizarte, Kern Pharma’s feeder club.
He will be followed at 16:18 later by the much more experienced Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL), lining up for the sixth time at the start of La Vuelta.

[{"updatedAt":"2026-08-22T16:14:48+02:00","pinned":false,"type":"liv","createdBy":"bvittek","id":51241,"title":"Following the tracks of Formula 1 legends","picto":"liv_chrono","year":2026,"createdAt":"2026-08-22T16:14:48+02:00","updatedBy":"bvittek","locale":"en","slug":"following-the-tracks-of-formula-1-legends","text":["“A very urban, very technical route, with plenty of speed and changes of pace”: this is how Kiko Garcia, technical director of La Vuelta 26, describes the route of the first stage. “It’s a time trial that obviously won’t decide the winner of La Vuelta, but it will show who is best equipped in terms of technique, explosive power and the ability to manoeuvre on a city circuit.”

[{"updatedAt":"2026-08-22T16:14:48+02:00","pinned":false,"type":"liv","createdBy":"bvittek","id":51241,"title":"Following the tracks of Formula 1 legends","picto":"liv_chrono","year":2026,"createdAt":"2026-08-22T16:14:48+02:00","updatedBy":"bvittek","locale":"en","slug":"following-the-tracks-of-formula-1-legends","text":["“A very urban, very technical route, with plenty of speed and changes of pace”: this is how Kiko Garcia, technical director of La Vuelta 26, describes the route of the first stage. “It’s a time trial that obviously won’t decide the winner of La Vuelta, but it will show who is best equipped in terms of technique, explosive power and the ability to manoeuvre on a city circuit.”

Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) is set to be the first rider on course, from 16:17, as he participates in his first Grand Tour. At 24, he is in his third season as a professional, after developing with Lizarte, Kern Pharma’s feeder club.
He will be followed at 16:18 later by the much more experienced Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL), lining up for the sixth time at the start of La Vuelta.

Motorsport enthusiasts will recognise the Monaco Grand Prix circuit, which forms a significant part of the route. With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).

[{"updatedAt":"2026-08-22T16:14:48+02:00","pinned":false,"type":"liv","createdBy":"bvittek","id":51241,"title":"Following the tracks of Formula 1 legends","picto":"liv_chrono","year":2026,"createdAt":"2026-08-22T16:14:48+02:00","updatedBy":"bvittek","locale":"en","slug":"following-the-tracks-of-formula-1-legends","text":["“A very urban, very technical route, with plenty of speed and changes of pace”: this is how Kiko Garcia, technical director of La Vuelta 26, describes the route of the first stage. “It’s a time trial that obviously won’t decide the winner of La Vuelta, but it will show who is best equipped in terms of technique, explosive power and the ability to manoeuvre on a city circuit.”
The route will be relatively flat, with an elevation gain of 59 metres over a total distance of 9.4 kilometres. Motorsport enthusiasts will recognise the Monaco Grand Prix circuit, which forms a significant part of the route. The riders will pass through the Place du Casino, the famous Fairmont bend and the Louis II tunnel before arriving on Boulevard Albert 1er, where the victory cries of drivers such as Ayrton Senna, Alain Prost, Michael Schumacher, Fernando Alonso, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli still echo."],"stage":1,"stageType":"PAS","highlight":false,"publicationAt":"2026-08-22T16:14:48+02:00","_id":"6dc5367e1bea2fcd9489b530f04836de5e10b1126404b676be27f94f51a18a6c","_bind":"publication_en-2026-1","_origin":"news-2026-1","_updatedAt":1787408089148,"_parent":"stage-2026:93bd5639e913abc271fb13124da9db9a6a602ca76973eeae9a729197feefbbdb","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:following-the-tracks-of-formula-1-legends","model":"news"},{"stageType":"PAS","stage":1,"highlight":false,"type":"liv","pinned":false,"updatedBy":"bvittek","id":51201,"year":2026,"text":["The start in Monaco features a very special participant: Monegasque rider Victor Langelloti (XDS Astana), the only rider from the Principality in the current professional peloton, who will begin his third appearance in La Vuelta on home soil.
“As a Monegasque, it is an honour to be able to ride La Vuelta at home and a source of pride to be able to wear this jersey”, says Langellotti, who won both the road race and the ITT at the national championships. “In 2009, when the Tour de France started from here, as a local cyclist I was able to accompany Alberto Contador’s Astana team at the team presentation. Now, riding with them and being able to start La Vuelta at home is incredible – something I could never have imagined.”"],"picto":"liv_interview","createdAt":"2026-08-22T15:56:25+02:00","slug":"a-very-special-day-for-langellotti","locale":"en","updatedAt":"2026-08-22T15:56:25+02:00","publicationAt":"2026-08-22T15:56:25+02:00","title":"A very special day for Langellotti","createdBy":"bvittek","_id":"588221766b8e155895d3a98ea3d5d30b373edc496335bdf41f2c84248ce6f020","_bind":"publication_en-2026-1","_origin":"news-2026-1","_updatedAt":1787406985239,"_parent":"stage-2026:93bd5639e913abc271fb13124da9db9a6a602ca76973eeae9a729197feefbbdb","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:a-very-special-day-for-langellotti","model":"news"},{"year":2026,"stageType":"PAS","picto":"liv_story","publicationAt":"2026-08-22T15:51:48+02:00","highlight":false,"type":"liv","updatedBy":"bvittek","title":"Welcome to Monaco","locale":"en","createdAt":"2026-08-22T15:51:48+02:00","stage":1,"updatedAt":"2026-08-22T15:51:48+02:00","slug":"welcome-to-monaco","id":51188,"createdBy":"bvittek","pinned":false,"text":["For the seventh time in 81 editions, and the fourth time in five years, La Vuelta is setting off from outside Spain. After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn.
With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. There are two former winners of La Vuelta: Primoz Roglic (2019, 2020, 2021, 2024) and Sepp Kuss (2023). Enric Mas, Joao Almeida, Jack Haig and Tadej Pogacar are the others top 3 finishers.Primoz Roglic also won the points standings (2019, 2020). He will be followed at 16:18 later by the much more experienced Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL), lining up for the sixth time at the start of La Vuelta.
The 184 contenders of this edition will start every minute, finishing wit some of the most awaited champions in this edition. Belgian icon Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) will go at 19:17. He will be followed by Spain’s rising star Ivan Romeo (Movistar). After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn.
With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn.
With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. A few weeks later, Cancellara was the first leader of the 2009 Vuelta after an ITT in Assen (the Netherlands)."],"_id":"7496e3db0d627eafa45ce6c2191a4a18fcfd19d6632c34680901e1ce9a9d78a6","_bind":"publication_en-2026-1","_origin":"news-2026-1","_updatedAt":1787406708698,"_parent":"stage-2026:93bd5639e913abc271fb13124da9db9a6a602ca76973eeae9a729197feefbbdb","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:welcome-to-monaco","model":"news"},{"createdAt":"2026-08-22T17:44:11+02:00","text":["Born in 2006, Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) is the youngest rider at the start of the 81st La Vuelta. He is 20 years and 154 days old today, four months younger than Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché). With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn.
With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. A few weeks later, Cancellara was the first leader of the 2009 Vuelta after an ITT in Assen (the Netherlands)."],"_id":"7496e3db0d627eafa45ce6c2191a4a18fcfd19d6632c34680901e1ce9a9d78a6","_bind":"publication_en-2026-1","_origin":"news-2026-1","_updatedAt":1787406708698,"_parent":"stage-2026:93bd5639e913abc271fb13124da9db9a6a602ca76973eeae9a729197feefbbdb","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:welcome-to-monaco","model":"news"},{"createdAt":"2026-08-22T17:44:11+02:00","text":["Born in 2006, Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) is the youngest rider at the start of the 81st La Vuelta. He is 20 years and 154 days old today, four months younger than Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché). With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn.
With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn.
With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort. After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn.
With the Gran Salida of La Vuelta 26, Monaco becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, after the Giro d’Italia (1966) and the Tour de France (2009).
Today’s ITT echoes the Grand Départ of the Tour de France 2009, when Fabian Cancellara took the Maillot Jaune after a 15.5 km effort.
